title: Leave it
translation: If changing something does no good, it's better to leave it alone.
original: {改|あらた}めて{益|やく}なきことは、{改|あらた}めぬをよしとするなり。
literal: As for things where changing them brings no benefit, not changing them is considered good.

notes.text: {益|やく}なし: 'useless, pointless'. Here {益|やく} is the older reading; modern Japanese reads the same kanji えき, as in {無益|むえき}.

notes.quote: 改めぬをよしとするなり
notes.text: ぬ here is the negative ず in its attributive form: 'not changing'. よしとす: 'to count as good'.
The whole section is one sentence. The text says nothing about what kind of change it means: customs, rules or anything else.
